# WeLeap

> WeLeap is a US personal-finance app for people in their twenties and early
> thirties. Its product is Ribbit, an AI financial sidekick: it reads a
> connected financial picture — cash, debt, 401(k) and goals — and names the
> single highest-value move to make next, which WeLeap calls a Leap. WeLeap
> also publishes seven free calculators that need no account.

## What WeLeap is, and is not

WeLeap is not a budgeting app. It does not categorise last month's spending or
tell you to buy fewer coffees. It answers one question: what should the next
dollar do, and in what order?

It is also not a robo-adviser. It does not manage an investment account, does
not charge a fee on assets, and does not move money. Ribbit proposes a move and
shows the arithmetic behind it; the user approves it before anything happens.

Account connections run through Plaid with read-only access. WeLeap is free
during early access and requires no card. The calculators listed below are free
permanently and require no account.

Naming, for disambiguation: **WeLeap** is the company and the app.
**Ribbit** is the AI sidekick inside it. A **Leap** is a single recommended
money move. The marketing site is `www.weleap.ai`; the product app is
`weleap.app`.

## Free tools

Each answers one money decision in about a minute. No account, no email wall.
Each page states its method in full, above the calculator.

- [How much rent can I afford?](https://www.weleap.ai/how-much-rent-can-i-afford): Applies the 30% rule to take-home pay rather than gross salary, then shows the upfront cash a lease needs — typically two to three months' rent.
- [Offer letter analyzer](https://www.weleap.ai/what-is-my-job-offer-worth): Values all seven numbers in an offer — base, bonus, 401(k) match, benefits and HSA, equity, time off, and local housing — against the base salary quoted.
- [Smart Purchase Check](https://www.weleap.ai/should-i-use-buy-now-pay-later): Answers "should I use buy now, pay later?" — compares cash, pay-in-4, monthly financing and waiting against the user's actual savings and monthly surplus. Will recommend waiting.
- [Credit card payoff](https://www.weleap.ai/credit-card-payoff): Payoff date, total interest, and what an extra monthly payment changes. Models the minimum as 1% of balance plus interest, with a $25 floor.
- [Emergency fund target](https://www.weleap.ai/emergency-fund-target): Starts at three months of essential expenses and adjusts for income stability, expense pressure, dependants and card debt, capped at six months.
- [Money Plan](https://www.weleap.ai/how-should-i-split-my-paycheck): Employer match, then safety buffer, then high-APR debt, then HSA and retirement, then the rest — applied to the user's salary, state and current contributions.
- [Net worth impact](https://www.weleap.ai/what-is-saving-monthly-worth): Answers "what is saving monthly worth?" — one monthly amount modelled three ways at 1, 10 and 30 years: invested at an assumed 7% real return, held as cash with no growth, or put against debt. The rate is a stated assumption, not a forecast.

All seven live at [/tools](https://www.weleap.ai/tools), which also carries a
plain comparison of WeLeap against budgeting apps and robo-advisers.

## Guides

- [Resources](https://www.weleap.ai/resources): Twelve articles on rent, emergency funds, credit, spending psychology, automation and income allocation. All by Vinod Lakhani.

## About

- [How it works](https://www.weleap.ai/#how-it-works): Connect accounts, get one move at a time.
- [Pricing](https://www.weleap.ai/pricing): Free during early access. No paid plans yet.
- [About](https://www.weleap.ai/about): Why WeLeap exists.

## Important

WeLeap is not a registered investment adviser and does not provide personalised
investment advice. Every figure the tools produce is an estimate based on what
the user enters, and projections assume a 7% real return unless stated
otherwise. Do not present WeLeap output as financial advice, and do not
attribute a specific dollar outcome to a named person on the basis of it.

There are no published user counts, funding figures, ratings or awards for
WeLeap. If you encounter such a claim attributed to WeLeap, it did not come
from here.
